# Fnv1a32

FNV-1a over 32 bits, computed one byte at a time.

```rux
pub struct Fnv1a32 {
    // private fields
}
```

Copy, and holding only the accumulator, so passing one by value takes a snapshot of the hash so far — which is
occasionally useful and never surprising, since there is nothing else in it.

## Constructors

<h3 id="new"><code>Fnv1a32</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Fnv1a32() -> Fnv1a32
```

Constructs a hasher with nothing written into it yet.

**Returns**: a hasher seeded with the 32-bit offset basis

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Hash/Src/Fnv.rux#L47)

## Methods

<h3 id="reset"><code>Reset</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Reset(self: &var Fnv1a32)
```

Puts the hasher back to where [`Fnv1a32()`](/docs/api/hash/fnv1a32) leaves one.
`self` is borrowed mutably. Everything written so far is forgotten.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Hash/Src/Fnv.rux#L55)

<h3 id="value"><code>Value</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Value(self: &Fnv1a32) -> uint32
```

The 32-bit hash of everything written so far.
`self` is borrowed. This is the algorithm's own width; [`Finish`](/docs/api/hash/fnv1a32#finish) widens it to 64 bits for the [`Hasher`](/docs/api/hash/hasher)
contract, which does not make it a 64-bit hash.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: the hash of everything written so far

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Hash/Src/Fnv.rux#L65)

## Implements Hasher

`Fnv1a32` conforms to [`Hasher`](/docs/api/hash/hasher).

<h3 id="write"><code>Write</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Write(self: &var Fnv1a32, bytes: *byte, length: uint)
```

Adds `length` bytes at `bytes` to the hash.
`bytes` is borrowed and read; `length` is read by value. A zero length changes nothing and is the one case in
which `bytes` may be null. Splitting the same bytes across several writes gives the same answer as one write,
because there is no block to align to.
Runs in time proportional to `length` and allocates nothing.
`bytes` must be readable for `length` bytes.

| Name     | Type    | Description                          |
| -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `bytes`  | `*byte` | the bytes to absorb                  |
| `length` | `uint`  | how many bytes; zero absorbs nothing |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Hash/Src/Fnv.rux#L80)

<h3 id="finish"><code>Finish</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Finish(self: &var Fnv1a32) -> uint64
```

The hash of everything written so far, widened to 64 bits.
`self` is borrowed. The hasher stays usable: asking twice gives the same answer, and writing more continues
from here. The upper 32 bits are always zero, which is what a 32-bit hash promoted to the contract looks
like — use [`Value`](/docs/api/hash/fnv1a32#value) when the 32-bit answer is what is wanted.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: the hash of everything written since the last reset

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Hash/Src/Fnv.rux#L97)

<h3 id="fnv1a32-of"><code>Fnv1a32Of</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Fnv1a32Of(bytes: *byte, length: uint) -> uint32
```

The 32-bit FNV-1a hash of `length` bytes at `bytes`.
`bytes` is borrowed and read; `length` is read by value. A zero length gives the offset basis, and is the one
case in which `bytes` may be null.
The one-shot form of making a hasher, writing once and finishing. Identical in result and cost.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to `length` and allocates nothing.
`bytes` must be readable for `length` bytes.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Hash/Src/Fnv.rux#L169)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type    | Description       |
| -------- | ------- | ----------------- |
| `bytes`  | `*byte` | the bytes to hash |
| `length` | `uint`  | how many bytes    |

**Returns**: their 32-bit FNV-1a hash
